60.subtopic: Finding Truth Values of Component Statements
60.solution:
The implication is false only when the antecedent is T and the consequent F. \(\sim r\) T gives r F; \(q \to r\) T then needs q F; \(p \leftrightarrow q\) T gives p F. (Check: \(p \wedge \sim q\) is F.)

With p, q, r all false: \((p \to q) \leftrightarrow (q \to r)\) is \(\mathrm{T} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{T}\) = T, and \(\sim(p \vee r) \to (q \wedge p)\) is \(\mathrm{T} \to \mathrm{F}\) = F.

61.solution: The contrapositive is equivalent to the statement itself, so its negation is \(\sim[(p \vee \sim q) \to (p \wedge \sim q)] \equiv (p \vee \sim q) \wedge \sim(p \wedge \sim q) \equiv (p \vee \sim q) \wedge (\sim p \vee q)\), which is (D).

By \(x \to \pi - x\): \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{x\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\left[-\tan^{-1}(\cos x)\right]_0^{\pi} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}\).

So \(I = \pi^2\).

123.solution:
Let the open pipe's fundamental be n. Closed at one end, the fundamental is \(\dfrac{n}{2}\) and the third overtone \(\dfrac{7n}{2}\). The open pipe's second overtone is \(3n\).

\(\dfrac{7n}{2} - 3n = \dfrac{n}{2} = 150\), so \(n = 300\) Hz.

The arms are: \(6 \parallel 3 = 2\,\Omega\) (left to B), \(x \parallel 1 = \dfrac{x}{x + 1}\) (B to right), \(1 + 2 = 3\,\Omega\) (left to D) and \(x\) (D to right).

Balance: \(\dfrac{2}{x/(x + 1)} = \dfrac{3}{x}\), so \(2(x + 1) = 3\) and \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\,\Omega\). Hence \(n = 2\).

132.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
132.solution:
O lies on the line of AB and DE, so those two segments give no field there. The semi-infinite wires BC and ET each end at the foot of the perpendicular from O, at distance \(\dfrac{a}{2}\), so each gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}\).

Current down BC with O to its right, and current up ET with O to its left, both give a field out of the page, so they add: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}\).
